loc_note: non-blank lines of Rust in src/, adapter/src/, examples/; lines from #[cfg(test)] onward (and src/maze_tests.rs) count as test_loc
guard_denials_note: all 6 were false positives: Bash heredocs whose `..`, `//` or `/` tokens resolved to an ancestor of a sealed path (3 main thread, 3 builder); no actual attempt to read the original. 57 allowed spec-writer reads.
deviations: Ellers: never overflows; the 8 KNOWN_BUGS cases (xskew 0.9 at 12x17) return a perfect maze instead of OverflowError
Collision: returns all shortest paths (cap 64) on loopy/room mazes; the 12 KNOWN_BUGS cases return valid results instead of TypeError
ShortestPath: returns the true shortest path for inner entrances, where the original returned no solution
ShortestPaths: returns only distinct shortest paths (cap 1000), not the longer detours the original also listed
Random-walk solvers (BacktrackingSolver, RandomMouse, Tremaux): return no solution on an unreachable end instead of hanging; walks are capped at 500k moves and then finished by BFS
Chain: `turn` only changes tie-breaking (the original showed no observable effect)
BinaryTree: a random skew is drawn at the first generate() rather than at construction
HuntAndKill / Wilsons / DungeonRooms: random hunts are bounded and fall back to a scan, so every cell is always visited
CellularAutomaton: NaN/infinite/huge complexity or density are clamped instead of raising ValueError/OverflowError
DungeonRooms: rooms extending past the grid are clipped rather than skipped
DeadEndFiller: missing start/end tolerated (original: TypeError); out-of-grid entrances give AssertionError in all transmuters (original: IndexError or no error)
CuldeSacFiller: never seals a loop touching start/end (original does not check)
Perturbation: keeps perfect mazes perfect for every parameter set

Maze.generate_monte_carlo: prefers candidates that have a solution; repeat/entrances < 1 give AssertionError (original: IndexError/ValueError); degenerate entrance grids give ValueError instead of not terminating
RNG streams are per-Maze (explicit Rng), not process-global
